subsystems.name: Senescent-cell biology
subsystems.role: the target: damaged cells that stop dividing but survive and leak inflammatory signals.

subsystems.name: Drug classes
subsystems.role: different molecules attack different survival pathways, so they are not interchangeable.

subsystems.name: Selectivity
subsystems.role: the core difficulty: killing senescent cells while leaving healthy dividing cells unharmed.

subsystems.name: Biomarkers
subsystems.role: without a way to measure senescent burden in a living person, trials cannot tell whether the drug worked.

subsystems.name: Clinical trial apparatus
subsystems.role: testing intermittent dosing in age-related disease rather than continuous treatment.
parts: endpoints such as walking speed or fibrosis scores

buildSteps.title: Map the survival pathway
buildSteps.detail: Identify which anti-apoptotic proteins a senescent cell depends on, since healthy cells rely on others.

buildSteps.title: Screen molecules
buildSteps.detail: Test compound libraries against senescent and non-senescent cells of the same tissue to find selective killers.

buildSteps.title: Validate in cell models
buildSteps.detail: Confirm that treated senescent cells die and that neighbouring healthy cells survive and keep dividing.

buildSteps.title: Test in aged animals
buildSteps.detail: Give the drug intermittently to old mice and measure clearance of senescent cells and changes in function or lifespan.

buildSteps.title: Check safety and pharmacokinetics
buildSteps.detail: Establish how long the drug stays in the body and whether it damages bone marrow, gut lining or other fast-dividing tissues.

buildSteps.title: Develop a human biomarker
buildSteps.detail: Find a blood or tissue measure of senescent burden that moves when the drug works.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Start with safety in older or ill patients, then test a specific disease such as lung fibrosis or kidney disease.

buildSteps.title: Move toward prevention
buildSteps.detail: If safety holds, trial intermittent courses in healthy older adults before disease appears.

prerequisites.why: p16 and SASP factors are measurable but inconsistent between tissues and people.
most candidates hit pathways healthy cells also use, which limits dose.
trials currently rely on functional endpoints, so negative results are hard to interpret.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term safety data for intermittent dosing
prerequisites.why: removing cells that also help wound healing and tumour suppression carries risk.
regulators and trial designs for treating ageing itself, rather than one disease, are still forming.

pathway.milestone: early-phase trials of repurposed drugs in specific diseases
pathway.unlocks: first human safety and dosing data.

pathway.milestone: validated biomarkers and larger controlled trials
pathway.unlocks: the ability to show cause and effect, not just correlation with ageing.

pathway.milestone: approval of a senolytic for one age-related disease
pathway.unlocks: a proof of concept that a whole drug class can follow.

pathway.milestone: preventive intermittent courses in healthy ageing
pathway.unlocks: shifting from treatment to delay of multiple diseases at once.
